editorial:
Eleventh Hour is the twelfth of seventeen Superman shorts in the Paramount cartoon series. Famous Studios made it, with Dan Gordon directing. Paramount released it on November 20, 1942. In the plot, Clark Kent and Lois Lane are held under house arrest as prisoners of war in Yokohama. Each night when the eleventh hour strikes, Superman sabotages a ship or bridge. Notices are posted warning that Lois will be executed if the sabotage continues. She is taken out for execution, and Superman rescues her. The music is credited to Sammy Timberg. It is an eight-minute Technicolor short.

The rights trap is the character. This is a 1942 film, so its print is not free by age alone. A work published in November 1942 would have its renewal window in its 27th and 28th year, so 1969-1970, with 1971 only as a late-filing check. I did not confirm from a Catalog of Copyright Entries page that no renewal was filed, so the print status stays open until someone checks. Superman is a separate underlying work, and I have not confirmed its rights status. Reusing the footage is a different question from making new Superman material.
faq: Is Eleventh Hour (1942) safe to reuse?

Not yet confirmed. The print's status depends on whether a renewal was filed in the 1969-1970 window (1971 for a late filing). I did not check the Catalog of Copyright Entries. Check the printed CCE Motion Pictures volumes first, using the links in the dossier. Separately, Superman the character is a different work, and its status is unverified.
Which version should I use if I want to share it?

The only archive.org upload I found is an unverified user upload dated 2026-10-14. The page shows no runtime and no rights statement. It is not a verified restoration. If you need quality, find a source with clear provenance and check whether it adds protected material such as new titles or a new score.
